newsitem.title: UK: UK sales healthy but below expectations in Dec-CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK sales healthy but below expectations in Dec-CBI.

text.p: British retail sales volumes in December were higher than the same month a year ago but growth fell well below expectations, the Confederation of British Industry said on Friday.
The CBI's December distributive trades survey found 52 percent of retail firms reported higher sales year-on-year while 19 percent said sales fell -- leaving a positive balance of 33 percent.
That was well below November's reading, which showed a balance of 48 percent of firms enjoyed sales growth.

The previous month's survey also showed a positive balance of 53 percent of retailers had expected December sales to rise compared with a year earlier. Perhaps once bitten twice shy, only a 32 percent balance expect January's sales to improve.

"Most retailers had a good Christmas," said Alastair Eperon, chairman of the CBI's distributive trades survey panel, noting that December's survey was measured against a large jump in the rate of sales growth a year ago.
"The majority of retailing sectors reporting positive sales growth suggests this Christmas was more than just a toy story," Eperon said.
The three-monthly average of sales suggests underlying growth remains strong.
The survey showed the biggest winners in December were booksellers and stationers, grocers, confectioners and specialist food stores. Footwear and leather shops were hit hardest.
Sales volumes in the wholesale sector slowed sharply year-on-year. A balance of only eight percent of firms saw sales volumes rise, down from 49 percent in November.
Meanwhile, motor traders reported no change in sales volumes in December compared with the Christmas month the year before. Traders said business was well above average for the time of year.
The CBI's trades survey canvasses 15,000 outlets of firms responsible for about 40 percent of employment in retailing, wholesaling and the motor trade.
